title: 어른께 말할 때: 드시다, 주무시다, 분, 댁
objective: By the end, you can swap common plain words (먹다, 자다, 있다, 이름, 나이, 집, 사람) for their honorific forms in short sentences about elders. You will also know not to use these words about yourself.
summary: Learn ten everyday honorific words that Koreans use when they talk to or about older people, bosses, and customers.

task.title: Use the honorific words
task.line: Read each item, then choose, write, or check the polite word that fits an older person or a boss.

words.meaning: to eat or drink (said about an older person)
words.exampleMeaning: Dad, would you like some more coffee?

words.meaning: to sleep (said about an older person)
words.exampleMeaning: Grandma is sleeping in her room right now.

words.meaning: to be (somewhere), to stay (said about an older person)
words.exampleMeaning: Is Mr. Kim in the office now?

words.meaning: name (of an older person or a customer)
person (polite word for an older person or a customer)

words.exampleMeaning: Is the manager's home far from the office?

words.meaning: words, what someone said (of an older person)
words.exampleMeaning: I listened carefully to what the teacher said and took notes.
This Saturday is my mother's birthday.

words.meaning: to be sick, unwell (said about an older person)
words.exampleMeaning: Grandma has been a bit unwell lately.

exercises: Choose the right word: ① 사장님은 지금 회의실에 (있어요 / 계세요). ② 아버지가 아침을 (드셨어요 / 먹었어요).
Write the honorific noun for each plain word: ① 이름 ② 나이 ③ 집 ④ 생일 ⑤ 사람 ⑥ 말
Fill in the blank with the past tense of the honorific word for 'sleep': 어젯밤에 할아버지가 일찍 ____.
Is the sentence correct and polite? Write Yes or No: ① 할머니, 이름이 뭐예요? ② 사장님 댁에 다녀왔어요. ③ 저는 매일 밤 11시에 주무세요. ④ 어머니가 감기 때문에 편찮으세요.
Rewrite the sentence with honorific words: 할아버지가 집에서 자요.
Answer in Korean: You meet your friend's grandmother. Politely ask her age.
answers: ① 성함 ② 연세 ③ 댁 ④ 생신 ⑤ 분 ⑥ 말씀
① No (이름 → 성함, 뭐예요 → 어떻게 되세요) ② Yes ③ No (do not use 주무시다 about yourself → 자요) ④ Yes
